events.label: birth
events.text: Born in Dordrecht, Netherlands.

evidence.quote: 29 September 1857 , in Dordrecht

events.text: Obtained doctorate in law at Leiden with a thesis on the colonies.

evidence.quote: He achieved his doctorate in September 1879

events.text: Made available to the Governor-General of the Dutch East Indies as a civil servant.

evidence.quote: On 20 August 1880 he was made available to the Governor-General

events.text: Travelled with his wife to Batavia, Dutch East Indies.

evidence.quote: With his wife Van Deventer travelled in September 1880 to Batavia by steamboat Prins Hendrik

events.text: Appointed court clerk at the Council of Justice in Amboina.

evidence.quote: appointed court clerk at the Raad van Justitie ( Council of Justice ) at Amboina in December 1880

events.text: Appointed court clerk at the Landraden of Amboina, Saparua and Wahoo.

evidence.quote: In June 1882 Van Deventer was appointed court clerk at the Landraden ( land boards ) of Amboina

events.text: Also appointed auditeur militair at the court-martial in Amboina.

evidence.quote: In June 1882 Van Deventer was appointed court clerk at the Landraden ( land boards ) of Amboina

events.text: Appointed member of the Council of Justice in Semarang.

evidence.quote: In March 1883 he was appointed member of the Council of Justice in Semarang

events.text: Joined the legal practice of Sloet van Hagensdorp and Van Oosterzee.

evidence.quote: That same year , 1885 , he quit his job at the Council of Justice and joined the legal practice
Van Deventer worked as a private lawyer from 1885 to 1888

events.text: Quit his job as member of the Council of Justice in Semarang.

evidence.quote: In April 1885 Van Deventer quit his job as a member of the Council of Justice in Semarang

events.text: Appointed lawyer and attorney at the Council of Justice in Semarang.

evidence.quote: In April 1885 Van Deventer quit his job as a member of the Council of Justice in Semarang
and was appointed lawyer and attorney at this Council of Justice

events.text: Ended his period as a private lawyer.

evidence.quote: Van Deventer worked as a private lawyer from 1885 to 1888

events.text: Took leave and travelled with his wife to Europe.

evidence.quote: In May 1888 he took a leave for Europe

events.text: Resumed his lawyer practice in the Dutch East Indies.

evidence.quote: He returned to the Dutch Indies on 11 May 1889 by steamboat Sumatra . He resumed his lawyers practice

events.text: Became commissioner of the limited liability company Hotel du Pavillon.

evidence.quote: He returned to the Dutch Indies on 11 May 1889
and also became commissioner of the limited liability company Hȏtel du Pavillon

events.text: Returned to the Dutch East Indies by steamboat Sumatra.

evidence.quote: He returned to the Dutch Indies on 11 May 1889

events.text: Appointed acting member of the Committee of Directors of the Dutch East Indian Railway Company.

evidence.quote: In September 1892 he was appointed acting member of the Committee of Directors

events.text: Promoted to first lieutenant in the Schutterij in Semarang.

evidence.quote: In July 1893 Van Deventer was promoted to the military rank of first lieutenant

events.text: Left for a second short stay in Europe.

evidence.quote: He left for a second short stay in Europe in May 1894

events.text: Left the Dutch East Indies permanently by steamboat Koningin-Regentes.

evidence.quote: He left the Dutch East Indies ( permanently ) in April 1897

events.label: article
events.text: Wrote the influential article Een Ereschuld (a debt of honour) in De Gids

evidence.quote: In 1899 Van Deventer wrote a very influential article , called Een Ereschuld ( a debt of honour ) in the Dutch magazine De Gids

events.text: Became member of the editorial board of De Gids.

evidence.quote: member of the editorial board of The Gids as of 1 January 1901

events.text: Accepted candidacy for the Schiedam electoral association; not elected.

evidence.quote: In June 1901 Van Deventer accepted his candidacy for the electoral association Schiedam

events.text: Appointed member of the Algemeen Nederlands Verbond.

evidence.quote: In June 1902 he was appointed
member of the Algemeen Nederlands Verbond ( General Dutch Covenant )

events.text: Began living at Surinamestraat 20, The Hague.

evidence.quote: He lived at Surinamestraat 20 , The Hague ( 1903–1915 )

events.text: Became member of the board of the Royal Netherlands Institute of Southeast Asian and Caribbean Studies.

evidence.quote: became a member of the board of the Royal Netherlands Institute of Southeast Asian and Caribbean Studies ( 1903 )

events.label: conference
events.text: Attended the meeting of the Institut Colonial International in London.

evidence.quote: ( 1903 ) and that same year attended the meeting in London of the Institut Colonial International

events.label: honour
events.text: Appointed knight in the Order of the Netherlands Lion.

evidence.quote: In September 1904 he was appointed knight in the Order of the Netherlands Lion

events.text: Elected member of the House of Representatives for Amsterdam IX.

evidence.quote: On 19 September 1905 Van
Deventer was elected as a Free-thinking Democratic member of the House of Representatives for the constituency Amsterdam IX

events.text: Not reelected; left the House of Representatives.

evidence.quote: Van Deventer was not reelected and left the House of Representatives on 21 September 1909

events.text: Elected to parliament again; appointed member of the Senate by the States of Friesland.

evidence.quote: Van Deventer was elected to be a member of parliament again on 19 September 1911

events.text: Made a journey of several months to the Dutch East Indies as a senator.

evidence.quote: In February 1912 Van Deventer made , as a member of the Senate , a journey of several months to the

events.label: founding
events.text: Founded the Kartini Foundation to establish girls' schools in the Dutch East Indies.

evidence.quote: In 1913 he founded the Kartini Foundation in order to be able to establish girl schools

events.text: Left the Senate after remaining a senator until this date.

evidence.quote: He remained a Senate member until 16 September 1913

events.text: Reelected member of the House of Representatives for Assen.

evidence.quote: 16 September 1913 , when he was reelected as a member of the House of Representatives

events.text: Appointed official delegate of the Netherlands at the International Opium Conference in The Hague.

evidence.quote: In June 1914 he was appointed official delegate of the Netherlands at the International Opium Conference held in The Hague

events.text: Ended residence at Surinamestraat 20, The Hague.

evidence.quote: He lived at Surinamestraat 20 , The Hague ( 1903–1915 )

events.label: illness
events.text: Became seriously ill with peritonitis and was nursed at a Red Cross hospital.

evidence.quote: In September 1915 Van Deventer became seriously ill

events.label: death
events.text: Died in The Hague at the age of 57.

evidence.quote: He died at the age of 57 on 27 September 1915
